hook: Greg Brockman helped write OpenAI's founding announcement in December 2015 and has run its engineering effort ever since, first as chief technology officer and then, from November 2023, as president. Before that he left MIT to join Stripe in its earliest days, when the payments company was still called dev slash payments, and stayed through its rise into a major engineering organization as chief technology officer. He testified to the Senate about AI policy as early as November 2016, years before the topic reached the mainstream, and he was reinstated as OpenAI's president within days of the company's November 2023 board crisis.

standing.watch: Everything unresolved in these records is unresolved in the same way. Every case listed sits at the filed stage, with docket monitoring active and no development recorded yet, so no ruling, outcome or settlement appears for any of them. The tracker dates several of the filings to September 2026, among them Bass v. OpenAI, LLC, United States v. OpenAI OpCo LLC, GRANT v. OPENAI INC, Smigelski v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC and The Seattle Times Company v. OpenAI Inc, while the entries for JIANG v. OPENAI GROUP PBC and Vredenburgh v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC carry no date. Nothing in the records describes a planned listing, a funding round or a valuation for OpenAI, since the company entries carry no figures. What comes next, on these records, is the docket, and whether any filed case moves beyond filing. Until then the site holds a president in place and a set of open complaints.
standing.record: The site's records add up to a single-company career with a long public tail. OpenAI appears twice under his name, once as a company he founded and once as a company he is an executive of, and no other company is listed for him. The legal record is a cluster of filings against OpenAI entities, including Bass v. OpenAI, LLC, United States v. OpenAI OpCo LLC, JIANG v. OPENAI GROUP PBC, GRANT v. OPENAI INC, Smigelski v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC, Vredenburgh v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC, and The Seattle Times Company v. OpenAI Inc. Each of those is marked filed, with docket monitoring active and no development recorded yet by this tracker. One further case on the page, Buist v. Anthropic, PBC, names Anthropic rather than OpenAI, so on these records it does not attach to his company. The pattern is a founder whose public footprint is his company and whose company's footprint is litigation, and the records supplied include no news stories naming him.
standing.standing: Greg Brockman stands as president and co-founder of OpenAI, the company he helped announce in December 2015 and whose engineering effort he has run since, first as chief technology officer and then, from November 2023, as president. The site records him both as a founder of OpenAI and as an executive of it, which places him at the center of the organization rather than at its edge. His position rests on continuity, since he was reinstated as president within days of the company's November 2023 board crisis and the title was confirmed in the company's November 29, 2023 leadership announcement. Before OpenAI he left MIT to join Stripe in its earliest days, when it was still called dev slash payments, and served there as chief technology officer until May 8, 2015. He also testified before the U.S. Senate Commerce Committee on artificial intelligence policy on November 30, 2016, years before the topic reached the mainstream. The records list no other company he controls or leads.

quick_facts: Co-founded OpenAI in December 2015 and served as its first Chief Technology Officer
Became President of OpenAI, a title confirmed in the company's November 29, 2023 leadership announcement
Left MIT to join Stripe in its earliest days, when it was still called dev slash payments, and stayed as Chief Technology Officer until leaving on May 8, 2015
Placed 6th in the 2007 Intel Science Talent Search for a paper on Ducci sequences, per his personal website
Testified before the U.S. Senate Commerce Committee on artificial intelligence policy on November 30, 2016
Has published peer-reviewed papers on combinatorics, including work on universal cycles of labeled graphs
